name: scroll-linked
title: Scroll linked
author: Eduardo Retana
description: Maps scroll progress to a fade, rise, scale, or rotate. CSS scroll-driven animations run first. Reduced motion shows the finished state.

meta.descriptionEs: Fade, subida, escala o giro siguen el avance del scroll. Si el navegador puede, lo hace con CSS. Con movimiento reducido se ve el estado final.

examples.title: Scroll ligado
examples.description: Fade, subida, escala o giro siguen el avance del scroll.

examples.title: Glosario
examples.description: Los diez términos de scroll, con demos propias.

api.name: preset
api.description: Default rise. Opacity and transform only.

api.name: range
api.description: Progress window on the timeline. Default [0, 1]. The CSS animation-range uses the same window.

api.name: timeline
api.description: view() follows this element. scroll() follows the scrollport, scroll(root) for the document. Default view.

api.name: container
api.description: Scrollport for the hook fallback. Omit to use the window.

docs: Clean-room scroll-linked wrapper. No Motion UI or Motion+ source. Supported browsers use animation-timeline view() or scroll() and an animation-range taken from range. Otherwise use-scroll-progress and useTransform map the same window onto opacity and transform. Reduced motion, via motion-preference, shows the finished state and does not animate. Answer no if the CLI asks to overwrite use-scroll-progress, motion-preference, or another file the host already has. The item ships no theme, cssVars, or fixed colors.
